title: Controlling Soil Pollution
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Walk round the school and home compound listing pollutants: wastewater, plastic, used chemical containers, oil. Used chemical containers are never handled by children or reused for food or water.

skills.key_step: The child names the causes of soil pollution in gardening and at home (too much fertiliser and chemicals, plastics, wastewater with soap and oil, used chemical containers, dumped rubbish) and safe controls (correct amounts, reduce, reuse and recycle plastics, wastewater into a soak pit, safe container disposal, compost).

floor.question: Name a way of managing plastic waste.

representations: a fertiliser packet and a pesticide label
steps: Choose a safe way to control it.
contexts: a home with a car wash

board.do: Draw a garden with a pipe of soapy water running onto it.
Ask what the soap and oil do to the soil.
Draw a soak pit for the wastewater.

misconceptions.ask: What can too much fertiliser do to the soil?
misconceptions.repair: Show the packet rate (a bottle top per hole); explain that the extra salts burn roots and wash into rivers.

misconceptions.ask: Why is polythene a problem in the soil?
misconceptions.repair: Dig up a polythene bag buried last term next to a buried leaf; one is unchanged.

misconceptions.ask: Which helps to control soil pollution?
misconceptions.repair: Ask where the smoke, ash and melted plastic go; burning moves the pollution into the air and soil.

listen_for: Wash it and use it for drinking water
misconceptions.ask: What should be done with an empty pesticide container?
misconceptions.repair: Read a pesticide label's disposal instructions with the class.

checks.question: Name two causes of soil pollution.
checks.answer: any two of plastics, too much fertiliser, chemicals, wastewater, oil

checks.question: How should household wastewater be disposed of?
checks.answer: into a soak pit or safely away from gardens
